title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_---0RF_0LB0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1LA1RD_---0RF_0LB0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open, and only looked at. At every visit of the head, in state A, to the left end, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s. The first blocks run through a short cycle and every cycle feeds into the blocks further right, like a counter whose digits are blocks of irregular, growing sizes. The rules of this counter were not derived.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 31,044 cells have been visited and 31,010 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: A list of blocks at every left-end visit
claims.text: At all 12,927 moments in the first 109 steps when the head, in state A, is at the left end of the tape, the tape is A>0 1^a1 0 1^a2 … 0 1^ak (10,342 times) or the same with the head on the first 1. At step 809,445,816 the list has 17 blocks, the largest 8,967.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The block-list structure is described here, but its rules were not derived or proved; this machine was left at a first analysis.

explainer.lede: Not known, and only looked at: the tape is a list of blocks of 1s which the head updates like a counter with irregular digits. The rules were not derived here.

sections.heading: A list of blocks
html: Stop the machine every time the head, in state A, is at the left end of the tape. The tape is then a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, for example at step 1,095

The first two blocks run through a short cycle (with the head on a 0, the first block is 2, 4, 5, 3, 2, 4, 5, 3, …), and each cycle changes the blocks further right; now and then a change carries all the way and the tail of the list is rewritten (for example the list 3 6 12 44 5 at step 1,919 is 2 4 8 26 18 15 at step 4,022). So the list behaves like a counter whose digits are blocks of growing, irregular sizes. At step 809,445,816 it has 17 blocks:

Not done. The next step is to derive the rules of one sweep for a general list (which blocks change, and by how much), check them against the run, and look for the invariant or the Collatz-type map they define. This machine was left at this first look.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.484). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 31,044 cells (26,214 left of the start, 17 right), with a density of 1s of 0.999.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, swept by the head and updated like an irregular counter; not analysed beyond its shape.
